steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Where can you find the function that pauses the project until any button is pressed?


Solution:

A controller.pauseUntilAnyButtonIsPressed() function should be added inside scene 0 condition of the callScene function definition at the top of the // choice menu comment. The function can be found by typing controller and a dot operator, then selecting the function from the code completion tool. A pair of parentheses () must be typed after for the function to run.


Ask the ninja: 

❓ What color might make the title of the project stand out against the splash screen?


Solution:

In the scene 0 condition of the callScene function definition under // text sprite, the second parameter in the setOutline function should be changed from 0 to a larger value. White (1) is used for the other text sprites in the project to create a clear contrast with the background.



Ask the ninja: 

❓ How can text “disappear” from the screen, without the sprite being destroyed?


Solution:

At the bottom of the choiceMenu function definition before the callScene function is called, text.setText(‘ ‘) should be added to remove “choose level” by resetting the value of the text sprite.


Ask the ninja: 

❓ What type of value is stored in the score variable?


Solution:

Inside the createVariable function definition, the text parameter of the textsprite.create function should be changed to convertToText(score) in order to convert the numerical value of the score variable into text. In the onOverlap event, the text parameter of the setText function should also be replaced with convertToText(score).
steps.instructions:
Fix the bugs in the code to create a working project!


When the project begins, the title of the project, “Labyrinth Legends,” should appear at the top of the splash screen. The choice menu should only appear after the user has pressed a button.


Once the user has selected a level and a tilemap appears, the “choose level” text should disappear.


The score in the top left corner of the project should show the value of the score variable as it updates.


Use the functions in the code menu and the code completion tool to create a working version of this project!

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 9 of Brown Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about adding User Interface (UI) features, such as splash and game over screens, user choice, and game narrative that can significantly improve the User Experience (UX) of a project. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 9:

badges.title: Screen Time
badges.description: Use a variety of pixel art techniques to create full-screen image assets to enhance the user experience in a project.

badges.title: An Asset for Every Season
badges.description: Create 160x120 full-screen image assets that can be layered on top of one another to create a variety of game screens.

badges.title: Flavor Text
badges.description: Use the Text Sprite extension to create custom scene titles, directions, and variable counters on screen.

badges.title: Choose Your Adventure
badges.description: Create a personalized experience for the user by changing scenes based on their responses.

badges.title: Reliable Narrator
badges.description: Use the Story extension to create narrative scenes that describe what’s happening in the project.

badges.title: Chain of Command
badges.description: Convert a number value to a string.

badges.title: Red Light Green Light
badges.description: Pause a project until any button is pressed to make screens remain as long as a user chooses.
